prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1420; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claimant reported a left turn collision at an intersection and states the other vehicle struck the driver's side as the claimant was completing the turn. Claimant is not represented by counsel and has given a recorded statement.

Entry 2: Police report was obtained and lists the claimant as the driver of the insured vehicle, with the other driver cited for failing to yield. The driver is named on the policy and coverage is confirmed.

Entry 3: Two independent witnesses at the scene were interviewed by phone and both describe the impact in the same sequence as the claimant. Scene photos were received and show damage consistent with a side impact.

Entry 4: Adjuster inspected the insured vehicle at the repair facility. The damage pattern lines up with the described impact, and no prior unrelated damage was noted during the inspection.

Entry 5: Claimant reports pain in the right shoulder and limited range of motion following the collision and was referred for an initial medical evaluation. Medical records indicate the injury type and force of the crash are a good match.

Entry 6: Claimant's medical history shows treatment for the same shoulder area within the last two years, and the treating provider notes that this earlier condition contributes to some of the current complaints. Adjuster has noted this for the injury evaluation.

Entry 7: A neighbor contacted the office and said they believed the vehicle had been damaged a few weeks before the reported loss. No photos or other support were provided, and the claim file has been flagged for follow-up with the repair records.

Entry 8: Treatment has followed a typical course of care, with frequency of visits tapering as the claimant improved. The claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation with the adjuster and the medical team.

Entry 9: Claimant is improving and is expected to return to normal activity shortly. Injury claim is under review pending the prior-condition apportionment and the outcome of the follow-up on the neighbor's report.
